This was an exact replacement fit for my refrigerator. After I replaced this unit I found out that this was not my problem. I placed my old filter cartridge back in and it leaked the same as before. As I looked carefully at the old cartridge in the sunlight I noticed a very fine crack at one of the ports that extended under the o-ring. The new cartridge ports looked thicker. The new replacement cartridge did not leak. The water and ice will work without a cartridge in place if you want. You just won't have filtered water and ice. When you pull your old cartridge out the housing has a bypass and seals off so no water will come out of the housing when removing the cartridge (or very little water as long as it's working properly).

The water dispenser on my 5-year-old Whirlpool Gold refrigerator suddenly began having problems one day. The water slowed to a trickle. At first I thought it might be the filter, which was due to be changed, but after swapping in a new filter, the problem was worse. I was getting no flow at all. After watching a few YouTube videos, I thought the issue might be a frozen water line. I opened the freezer door for awhile (I put heavy cardboard over the opening to keep the contents as cold as possible) to allow the line to defrost, if that was, in fact, the problem. That yielded no results. I also verified that the ice maker was not making ice. I then reached out to Whirlpool - they were very responsive over Twitter, and even gave me a call, but they seemed totally clueless with little to offer other than reading canned text from a customer service rep manual (clearly those I was dealing with had little or no plumbing experience). More research led me to conclude that it might be the water filter housing. It was a bit of a gamble as I wasn't certain I'd be able to return this, but if it worked, it would save me from paying $250+ for a repair guy. I decided to go for it, and I'm glad I did. Replacing the water filter housing completely solved the problem.

When I inserted a new filter I got no flow through the water dispenser on the fridge. After removing the filter I could see a slow drip coming from the filter housing. After researching a bit online it seemed like the housing itself was a common failure point so I took a shot and ordered it. I figured it was cheaper than a service call.

After removing the old housing I dismantled it and found the reason that one no longer worked. You could see the valve stop for the filter input was weakened by years of water flowing past it. See pictures for more info.

It took less than an hour to install the new part and I didn't even have to access the back of the fridge.

Water slowed to a trickle. Was sure the water inlet valve was bad. Kept watching different repair videos and found out the culprit was indeed the water filter housing. Removed the filter and water shot out and hit me in the face. BAD HOUSING!
Watched two videos about replacing this part. One showed doing the replacement through the bottom front of the fridge. Video two showed removing front grill and rear cardboard panel. Video 2 applied to our particular model Whirlpool fridge. It took an hour to replace this water filter housing. That included vacuuming and light cleaning while it was pulled out from the wall.
Just take your time and you can save yourself probably an easy $150-250 in repair costs. Even if you don't have all the tools in the video, go buy some cheap nut-drivers and or a 1/4 inch socket set - it will make this very easy.

Too bad Whirlpool does not mention this problem in their troubleshooting. The old filter housing worked with the old model filters but would not work with the newer replacement model filters. Discovered after extensive troubleshooting that the old filter housing and the new replacement filters do not properly fit together. The new filters will not fully engage the needle/pin valves in the back of the older filter housing even though the filter fully inserts and locks into place. I ordered this newer filter housing and it fixed the problem. The newer filters fit much better into this newer filter housing. The OEM's make no mention of this and they state that the the newer/latest model filters are direct replacements. I discovered this is not true.  If you are having filter issues I would recommend replacing the filter housing as there may be an issue with proper fit. I tried three different filter brands of the same model before investigating the filter housing. Now the filters work. Hope this helps.
